title: Common normal constants and induction of finite semilinear scheme actions
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $I$ be a nonempty finite set. For each $i\in I$ let $F_i/e$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-pc-field-tower], let a finite group $J_i$ act on $F_i$ by $e$-automorphisms, and let $V_i$ be a finite-type $F_i$-scheme with a compatible semilinear $J_i$-action. Let $B_i$ be an $e$-scheme and $v_i:V_i\to B_i$ a $J_i$-invariant $e$-morphism [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There are a finite normal extension $K/e$ with embeddings $F_i\hookrightarrow K$, a finite group $G$ with a surjection $G\to A=\operatorname{Aut}_e(K)$, and subgroups $\Gamma_i\leq G$ with surjections $\Gamma_i\to J_i$. The two actions on $F_i$ agree, so $\Gamma_i$ acts diagonally on $W_i=V_i\times_{F_i}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The extension $K^G/e$ is purely inseparable. The induced scheme $Y_i=G\times^{\Gamma_i}W_i$ exists: it is the disjoint union of copies of $W_i$ indexed by left cosets of $\Gamma_i$, with scalar structure on the copy represented by $g$ twisted by the image of $g$ in $A$; the relation is $(g\gamma,w)\sim(g,\gamma w)$. Left multiplication gives a semilinear $G$-action, and $[g,w]\mapsto v_i(\operatorname{pr}_1w)$ defines an invariant $e$-morphism $Y_i\to B_i$. For every geometric point $b$ of $B_i$, if the geometric fibre of $v_i$ at $b$ is a nonempty single $J_i$-orbit, then the geometric fibre of $Y_i\to B_i$ at $b$ is a nonempty single $G$-orbit. If $v_i$ sends every generic point to a generic point with finite residue extension, the same is true of $Y_i\to B_i$. Finite morphisms and generic points use [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-sc-generic-point], [def-weil-residue-field]; geometric fibres use [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Normal for a finite field extension means that every irreducible polynomial over $e$ with a root in $K$ splits in $K$; no separability is assumed.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, contracted products and diagram (2.b). Agent-formulated finite-family semilinear version: take a common finite normal K/e and use the groups of compatible pairs in Aut_e(K) times J_i before induction. This formulation makes the common field and its action explicit; it is a general induction construction, with no alteration, resolution or SNC existence conclusion.
